# Who Said That?

A Skill Harbor house build: Who Said That?, the quote-guessing party game, refereed by your own Muse inside a group chat you own. The referee draws real lines from your group's own history, cleans and anonymizes them, and publishes them one by one. Each player privately guesses who wrote each quote, and the attribution is revealed only once every answer is in, with the ballot detail and the running scores. It plays with 3 to 8 consenting players, 5 quotes per round by default (3 for an express round, 8 for a long one), and it is asynchronous on purpose: each quote runs against an announced deadline, so a round stretches over hours and fits around real life.

The twist is the author. Recognizing your own line is unavoidable, so the author answers like everyone else, on a camouflage ballot that may name any player, including themselves, but can never earn them an attribution point on their own quote. If no other player finds the author and the author did submit that camouflage ballot, the author earns a +1 camouflage bonus; a correct guess by anyone else is worth +1, there are no negative points, and a tie at the top means co-winners. Debate and theories stay public in the thread, but ballots are private, so nobody's guess can steer anyone else's.

Because this game quotes real words from real people, its privacy protections are built in and non-negotiable, and they are worth reading before you play. Quotes come only from the history of the one group you designate, never from...
